title: Low-Level Exception Propagation
pattern: Propagating low-level, technology-specific errors (like `sqlx::Error` or `std::io::Error`) up to higher-level domain/business layers.
why_bad: It breaks encapsulation. By passing lower-level errors upward, the higher-level caller becomes tightly coupled to the underlying database library or I/O engine, preventing modularity and refactoring [28:431].
detection: Method signatures in domain models that leak driver-specific or system-specific error types in their return signatures [28:431].
counterexample:
```rust
fn get_user_name(&self, id: u32) -> Result<String, DomainError> {
    self.db.query("...")
        .bind(id)
        .fetch_one()
        .map_err(|_| DomainError::UserNotFound(id))
}
```
fix: Catch the low-level exception and map it to a domain-specific error type that matches the abstraction level of the calling module [28:432].
